result.title: Exact Scaling Laws for a Random-Features Bigram Model
result.summary: Understanding neural scaling laws is increasingly important for theory and practice, yet first-principles explanations remain limited even in simple settings. In this work, we study capacity-limited scaling in a bottlenecked bigram model with power-law (Zipf) token statistics, viewed as an analytically tractable toy model of a large language model. Fixed random embeddings serve as a proxy for representational capacity and induce an explicit bottleneck of width, allowing us to derive scaling laws for prediction regret as a function of model width, vocabulary size, and the Zipf exponent. Our results complement recent theoretical accounts based on optimization dynamics by isolating scaling due purely to representational constraints. In the appropriate regime, the theory recovers the functional form of classical neural scaling laws and suggests that heavy-tailed language statistics may underlie both optimization- and capacity-driven scaling. Experiments natural language datasets (WikiText2, OpenWebText) closely match the predicted curves.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在具有 Zipf 词频统计的瓶颈式 bigram 玩具模型上，把固定随机嵌入当作表示容量的代理，推导出预测遗憾关于模型宽度、词表规模和 Zipf 指数的精确 scaling law，并用 WikiText2、OpenWebText 上的实验验证曲线吻合。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把 scaling 归因于纯表示容量约束而非优化动态，可能为 LVR 中 latent 宽度瓶颈、容量受限与信息坍缩的度量与评价提供概念线索，但对象是纯文本 bigram，迁移性待核查。
